citation.authors: Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, Tighiouart H et al

cited_by.title: Kidney disease, the APOL1 gene and the eGFR race adjustment

record.population: 8,254 participants (31.5% Black) for the creatinine equation and 5,352 (39.7% Black) for creatinine plus cystatin C; validated in 4,050 (14.3% Black)
record.design: Development and validation of eGFR equations against measured GFR
record.finding: The current equation with a race term overestimated measured GFR in Black participants by a median of 3.7 mL/min/1.73 m2 and slightly in others (0.5). Omitting the race term underestimated it in Black participants by 7.1. A new race-free creatinine equation underestimated in Black participants by 3.6 and overestimated in non-Black by 3.9. Creatinine plus cystatin C equations were more accurate with smaller differences between groups.
record.note: US data; funded by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases.
